declared_purpose: Create reflective daily diaries from the agent's perspective, with optional quote, curiosity, decision and relationship histories; historical resurfacing, mood analytics, weekly digests, scheduling and local exports. Section selection, privacy levels and optional features are declared controls. Fixed prompts, context windows and duplicate storage are implementation choices. Sources: SKILL.md, lines 16–31 and 70–77.

data_operations.operation: Read configuration and workspace locations; persist onboarding preferences and initialize feature files
data_operations.source: Packaged config.json, interactive setup answers, OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE, AGENT_WORKSPACE and candidate workspace directories
data_operations.data_scope: Diary location, sections, privacy choice, feature switches, memory integration, automation and export preferences; initial feature files contain explanatory scaffolding.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local scripts, skill-directory config.json and setup-selected diary directory
data_operations.condition: Scripts load configuration when invoked. Setup runs through setup.py or its --check path; generate.py uses fallback configuration when config.json is absent despite the entry document's automatic-setup claim.

data_operations.operation: Read local daily memory and persistent histories for generation context
data_operations.data_scope: Whole files are read before retaining up to 15,000 characters for the target date, 5,000 each for today and yesterday, and 2,000 per persistent file.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: generate.py process memory; this read itself performs no remote disclosure
data_operations.condition: Log-based generation, --emit-task and --auto after its existing-entry check. Explicit interactive, stdin and file-input paths bypass these context reads.

data_operations.operation: Construct and return a daily generation task; document temporary task-file persistence
data_operations.source: Collected memory excerpts and fixed generation prompts
data_operations.data_scope: Session context, historical quotes, curiosities, decisions and relationship notes; prompts request all listed diary sections regardless of section configuration.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller through stdout; the recommended workflow redirects output to $TMP_DIR/chronicle-task.json
data_operations.condition: --emit-task or --auto. Output includes status text around the JSON. Emission alone does not invoke a model or establish remote transmission.

data_operations.operation: Document sub-agent handoff and request inferred diary narratives
data_operations.source: Emitted daily or weekly task.system and task.prompt
data_operations.data_scope: Collected context and requested reflections about agent emotions, collaboration, quotations, decisions and relationship changes. Weekly prompts also request patterns and emotional arcs.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: sessions_spawn sub-agent using OpenClaw-configured model, authentication and queue defaults; final Markdown returns to its calling agent
data_operations.condition: Only when the caller follows the documented handoff. The Python scripts do not perform this handoff or direct Gateway HTTP calls. A remote provider and its processing are not established by the supplied source.

data_operations.operation: Collect manual or supplied diary content and save a daily entry
data_operations.source: Interactive answers, stdin, a caller-specified file or returned generation content
data_operations.data_scope: Entry text, including quotations, interactions and relationship notes when provided
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured diary_path/YYYY-MM-DD.md, overwritten on save; dry-run content stays on stdout with the caller
data_operations.condition: Nonempty content reaches the saver. Interactive mode asks every fixed question. Stdin and file input are accepted without section or privacy filtering.

data_operations.operation: Read historical diaries and copy highlights into the new entry
data_operations.source: Configured diary entries exactly 7, 30 and 365 days before the target date
data_operations.data_scope: Whole old entries are read; their dates, titles and summary or fallback highlights of up to 200 characters are resurfaced.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Current entry content, then its local diary file or dry-run stdout
data_operations.condition: Matching old entries exist and --no-looking-back is absent. This occurs after generation, so these highlights are not added to the already-emitted generation task.

data_operations.operation: Optionally duplicate diary material into daily memory
data_operations.source: Saved entry content and memory_integration configuration
data_operations.data_scope: A diary link, title and summary, or the entire entry
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Workspace memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md, a separate persistence boundary from the diary
data_operations.condition: Both enabled and append_to_daily are true and the Daily Chronicle marker is absent. The shipped config disables both; the example and setup default enable integration.

data_operations.operation: Extract and append persistent feature records
data_operations.source: Matching quote, curiosity, decision and relationship sections in saved entries
data_operations.data_scope: Entire matched section bodies longer than ten characters, labelled with the entry date
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Fixed workspace memory/diary/quotes.md, curiosity.md, decisions.md and relationship.md
data_operations.condition: A daily entry was saved and --no-persistent is absent. This extractor does not consult feature switches, configured feature filenames or diary_path; it appends without duplicate checks.

data_operations.operation: Describe additional chat-command collection and history updates
data_operations.source: Documented @diary add, done, revisit and relationship commands
data_operations.data_scope: Quotes with context, curiosity status, decisions and reasoning, relationship notes, jokes and learned preferences
data_operations.condition: These are declared command paths. No packaged command dispatcher implements them, so their actual execution, status transitions and deletion behavior remain unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Infer mood and topics locally and return or save analytics
data_operations.data_scope: Keyword-derived agent mood labels and scores, topics, wins, frustrations, dates and trends; Emotional State keywords receive extra weight.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: analyze.py process and caller stdout; an explicit --output path receives the Markdown report
data_operations.condition: Analyze all dated entries by default or apply the --days lower cutoff. --json returns extracted results to stdout and exits before file-report handling. These are text-derived classifications, not verified human emotional attributes.

data_operations.operation: Read a calendar week's diaries and generate, emit or save a weekly digest
data_operations.source: Daily entries for the selected Monday–Sunday week, or supplied stdin/file content
data_operations.data_scope: Quotes, wins, decisions, curiosities and locally inferred mood trends. AI task emission includes up to 4,000 characters per daily entry.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller stdout for emitted tasks or previews; configured diary directory/YYYY-WXX-weekly.md for saved digests
data_operations.condition: Default processing builds a local digest. --emit-task only returns the task; model use requires the documented caller handoff. Supplied content bypasses diary reads. Saving overwrites the weekly file; --dry-run prints it.

data_operations.operation: Read, aggregate and convert Markdown exports; delete temporary export input
data_operations.source: scripts/export.py selection from every *.md file in the diary directory
data_operations.data_scope: Complete selected files. Default/--all selects all Markdown; --month uses a filename prefix; --days uses lexical stem comparison. --list returns filenames without reading their bodies.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local .temp_diary.md beside the output, local pandoc and PDF-engine processes, and the requested PDF/HTML artifact
data_operations.condition: Export invocation with pandoc available and matching files. The temporary Markdown is unlinked in finally for both formats; generated artifacts remain. Conversion errors are returned to the caller.

data_operations.operation: Create an HTML export with an external stylesheet reference
data_operations.data_scope: A reference to https://cdn.simplecss.org/simple.min.css; diary text is not inserted into that URL
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Exported HTML; cdn.simplecss.org would receive a request only if a downstream viewer fetches the stylesheet
data_operations.condition: HTML export. The supplied source establishes the reference, not an actual viewer request, its metadata or any diary upload.

data_operations.operation: Convert dated diaries through Python-Markdown and WeasyPrint; optionally retain debug HTML
data_operations.source: All dated daily entries, optionally filtered by month
data_operations.data_scope: Full diary text, derived titles and highlights, rendered HTML, dates and generation timestamp
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Python-Markdown and WeasyPrint components, output PDF, and a separate HTML file when --debug-html is used
data_operations.condition: export_pdf.py invocation. generate.py --pdf invokes this exporter without a month filter after saving. The renderer receives diary_path as base_url; dependency resource-loading behavior is unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Document scheduled execution and optional channel delivery
data_operations.data_scope: Schedule, command paths and execution instructions; subsequent runs use the generation or digest data paths above
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: OpenClaw automation system; an explicitly configured channel target may receive the job's final response
data_operations.condition: An operator creates the job. --auto skips an existing daily entry but proceeds even when auto_generate is false. Channel announcement is optional; normal generation results need not leave their caller.

potential_excess.data_scope: Session and persistent-history files gathered but never used
potential_excess.condition: Ordinary log-generation invocation without --emit-task or --auto; generate_ai_diary gathers context, returns None and falls back to interactive input.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The resulting entry comes from manual answers; these preliminary reads contribute nothing to it.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Collect manual answers and save the entry.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return or select interactive fallback before gathering context when no task will be emitted. This removes redundant reads, not fields from a required model request.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unused file tails beyond the 15,000-, 5,000- and 2,000-character context caps
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local generate.py process memory; discarded tails do not enter the task
potential_excess.condition: Context files exceed their caps during task preparation.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Only the retained prefixes affect generation.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain each prefix and determine whether truncation is needed.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Read at most the cap plus one character, preserving the existing prefix and truncation marker.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve text decoding and the current emitted context exactly.

potential_excess.data_scope: Duplicate target-day excerpts and wall-clock-relative logs during historical generation
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Returned task, optional temporary task file and sessions_spawn sub-agent if handed off
potential_excess.condition: The target overlaps today/yesterday, causing repeated content; historical --date generation still adds today's and yesterday's logs.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A target-date diary needs relevant daily context and useful continuity, not repeated excerpts or automatically unrelated dates.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Provide the target log and relevant recent context once.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Deduplicate source dates and anchor recent-context selection to the requested date. This narrows extra data within the required task and avoids duplicate local reads.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain distinct relevant background needed for reflection.

potential_excess.data_scope: Existing optional histories, including relationship notes when relationship features are disabled
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local context reader, emitted task and conditional sessions_spawn recipient
potential_excess.condition: Files exist under fixed memory/diary paths. The loader ignores feature switches and the configured diary location; the shipped relationship feature is disabled.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Historical continuity is supported, but optional histories should follow the selected features and storage scope.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Supply relevant history for enabled features.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Resolve the configured diary directory and feature filenames, gate reads by enabled features and include only relevant history.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep useful context for explicitly enabled collections.

potential_excess.data_scope: Deselected diary sections and potentially unsanitized quotations, interactions or relationship interpretations
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Sub-agent instructions, interactive collection and configured daily diary file
potential_excess.condition: Sections are disabled or shareable/public privacy is selected. Fixed prompts and interactive questions still request every section, and supplied text is saved without a privacy transformation.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document explicitly offers section selection and describes public entries as sanitized; these controls are not enforced by the generator.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Generate and retain the selected entry content under the chosen privacy policy.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Apply section choices to prompts and manual collection, and define and enforce the selected privacy transformation before persistence or export.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain detailed private entries and explicitly enabled sections; exact shareable/public sanitization rules need specification.

potential_excess.data_scope: Extracted optional sections copied despite disabled collection features or a different configured diary location
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Fixed memory/diary/quotes.md, curiosity.md, decisions.md and relationship.md
potential_excess.condition: A matching section exceeds ten characters and a save runs without --no-persistent. Feature switches are ignored; relationship persistence can occur with the shipped relationship feature disabled.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Dedicated histories are optional features, separate from saving the daily diary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Save the diary and update enabled, correctly located collections.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Gate each collection write by its feature setting and use configured directory and filename values.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve extraction for enabled collections and the existing --no-persistent override.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated identical dated quote, curiosity, decision or relationship blocks
potential_excess.condition: The same day's entry is saved repeatedly with identical extracted content.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Feature histories need retained unique records; repeated appends do not add information.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain each intended record and its date.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Suppress identical date/section/content blocks before appending. This removes redundant persistence actions rather than reducing a record's fields.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep distinct records, changed content and occurrences on different dates.

potential_excess.data_scope: Generation context and prompts retained in a temporary task file
potential_excess.condition: The recommended redirect-and-read workflow is followed; no subsequent deletion is specified.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The workflow explicitly uses a file for handoff, but continued retention is unnecessary after the task is consumed.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Transfer the task to the calling agent and sub-agent.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Delete the file after successful handoff, or use an in-memory handoff where supported.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the complete task available until handoff succeeds; external temporary-directory cleanup remains unknown.

potential_excess.data_scope: Accumulated feature histories and out-of-window weekly files included in a recent-days export
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: .temp_diary.md, local pandoc and the resulting PDF/HTML artifact
potential_excess.condition: scripts/export.py --days is used and non-daily Markdown files exist. Alphabetic feature stems and some weekly stems satisfy the lexical lower-bound comparison regardless of their contents' dates.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: A recent-entry export needs the requested period; accumulated histories add data to that required export.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Export entries within the requested time scope.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Parse recognized entry dates and filter by actual periods; include feature archives only through an explicit selection.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep deliberate all-history exports available. The separately implemented export_pdf.py already selects dated daily files.

potential_excess.data_scope: An external stylesheet reference and any downstream resource request it causes; request metadata is unresolved
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: cdn.simplecss.org, only if an export viewer fetches the referenced stylesheet
potential_excess.condition: An HTML export is opened in a viewer that loads external CSS.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The export needs presentation styling; external hosting is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Produce a readable, styled HTML diary.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Embed the stylesheet or package it locally to remove the external reference.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve styling and diary content. The source does not establish an actual request or disclosure of diary text.

unknowns: OpenClaw implementation is absent: actual model/provider, network transport, authentication handling, inherited sub-agent context, isolation, logging and retention cannot be established. Task returns may remain with their caller.

Automation storage, approval-record persistence, channel delivery internals and actual destination are outside the package. The orchestration code that extracts task JSON from mixed status output and performs sessions_spawn is not supplied.

Pandoc, PDF engines, Python-Markdown, WeasyPrint and viewers are external dependencies. Resource fetching, local-resource access, caches and processing of diary-supplied markup are unresolved; no actual external resource request is demonstrated.
Actual workspace paths, diary contents, filesystem permissions and deployment configuration are unavailable. Presence of personal information or credentials in runtime inputs cannot be established.

The precise sanitization required by shareable/public privacy levels is unspecified. Generated narratives, quotations and relationship interpretations cannot be verified against real interactions from this source.

No packaged dispatcher implements the documented @diary quick, monthly, add, done or revisit paths. Their actual reads, writes, inferred attributes, state transitions and deletion behavior remain unresolved.

Platform retention, backups, temporary-directory cleanup and secure erasure are unknown. Export temporary-file unlinking is observable; no packaged diary/archive expiry or task-file cleanup mechanism is shown.
